title: Inventors and Entrepreneurs

alignment.course_outcome: CO1 - Discuss the fundamentals of entrepreneurship

template_credit: Simple Accordion interaction template by Montse Anderson, elearningdesigner.com

illustration.subject: A split scene with an inventor refining a carbon-conversion prototype in a laboratory and an entrepreneur connecting it to industrial customers, operations and delivery across a bridge
illustration.composition: Two contrasting halves joined by a bright validation bridge
illustration.style: Blueprint-meets-editorial illustration with precise equipment and energetic market-side motion

case: Case connection: Breathe Applied Sciences demonstrates that technical novelty must be joined to cost, industrial-process, customer and regulatory clarity.
misconception: Common mistake: Assuming every inventor is an entrepreneur, every entrepreneur must invent, or a patent proves market value.
application: For a patented engineering device, list one technical, customer, economic and delivery question that must be validated.

sources.locator: Unit I, I.6 Inventors and entrepreneurs
sources.use: Role distinction, validation bridge and Breathe Applied Sciences case

sources.source: Startup and New Venture Management, Aurangabadkar and Singh
Launching New Ventures: An Entrepreneurial Approach, Kathleen R. Allen
